chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Oklahoma's musicians and the Pettiford family
summary: Oklahoma produced Simmons, Wardell Gray and the Pettifords including Harry, Ira and Alonzo.

blocks.x: Now, one thing that they're interested in is the whole idea of Oklahoma as an historical place for music. And I think I would include in my question the whole Southwest...
Because I don't think you can just pinpoint it to one area. Although you might want to start with Oklahoma and then talk about the whole Southwest.

Well, as far as Oklahoma is concerned, there wasn't too much happening there, except that a lot of good musicians came out of Oklahoma, you know, like John Simmons and Wardell Gray and several other people...

Oscar Pettiford; well, the whole family of Pettifords was from there. They had some trumpet players was out of sight, too. And a tenor player, Harry Pettiford; pshew, he was something else on the saxophone.

Well, he sounded like a modern Prez, but one with knowledge. You see, Prez played with feeling, and he had some beautiful things coming put. But Harry Pettiford played from knowledge, and he knew what he was playing. There wasn't no bullshit in what he was doing. And he could do what he wanted to do, you know.
But the whole Pettiford family was something...
I guess the trumpet player was named Ira -- Ira Pettiford?
Yeah, Ira. That was one. And he had another brother named Alonzo who played trumpet. And he was out of sight, too, man. He was very good. I think he got TB and died or something.
Did you know the father, Doc Pettiford?
Drums. And his wife played the piano, I think it was...whatever it was. And they had a daughter named Marge who played alto. Now, do you know her?
She played pretty good. She played pretty good. She didn't play like the boys could play, but she played pretty damn good. Yeah, I used to like to hear her
